name: Temple of Apollo Epicurius at Bassae
description: High in the Arcadian mountains of southern Greece, at about 1,130 metres, stands a remote temple to Apollo, god of healing and the sun, built around the mid-5th century BC. It is one of the best-preserved Greek temples, and it holds the oldest known Corinthian capital. Its unusual design includes a continuous sculpted frieze running around the inner chamber.
